strings.help.1: Press the mic button and start reading; the app finds the surah by itself (you can also choose it above). Pressing ■ ends the session and saves it.
strings.help.2: Words open as you read: green = correct, red = wrong/skipped (with a warning word), purple = hint/stuck. The blinking blue box = the word you should read now.
strings.help.3: Pause with the Pause button, look at the red words and listen, then press the same button to continue. If you like, read again from an earlier ayah to fix the mistake; the app will follow from there.
strings.help.4: When you finish one surah and start the next (or any other surah) the app moves there by itself — it follows as long as you read.
strings.help.5: The eye button switches between reading from the text (all text shown) and from memory (text hidden).
strings.help.6: If you are stuck press Hint, or keep silent (as many seconds as set in "Alafasy starts after a pause" above, {wait} at first): Mishary Alafasy will recite on from there and the words open in purple. When you start reading again (or press Pause/Stop) he stops and the app listens to you. Press and hold the hint button to open the rest of the ayah.
strings.help.7: Tap a red word to hear what you read and what you should have read — both with the surrounding words. If you read it correctly press ✓.
strings.help.8: Words where you made a mistake or got stuck in an earlier session stay light to dark red; after reading them correctly from memory {clear} times in a row the mark goes away.
strings.help.9: If you think a mark is wrong (when not recording, or in the Progress tab) tap the red box: listen to what you read and press ✓ Wrong mark — remove. The mark goes away and reading it that way will not be flagged again.
strings.help.10: In the Progress tab every surah has a coloured strip by ayah — you can see at a glance which ayahs are weakest (dark red). Tap a box to open that ayah below.
strings.help.11: On the phone: the model (about 19 MB) downloads the first time, then it works without internet. All data stays on this phone — you can back it up to a file from the Progress tab. Automatic checking can be wrong; it is not a replacement for a teacher.
